title: ops-alley-seller-qualifier-deck-annotated-draft
body:
Purpose: quick annotated slide deck for field sellers to qualify platform/ops buyers (platform engineering, SREs, infra PM) in 10 minutes; give a technical runway and fast objections -> demo checklist. This is intentionally concise, heavily annotated with speaker prompts and explicit follow-ups.

Slide 1 — Ops Alley opener
- Title: Ops Alley: fast qualify for platform & SRE buyers
- Speaker prompt: "Thanks — this is a 10 minute technical qualifier to understand where your team will care most: latency guarantees, predictable throughput, or private deployment controls."
- One-liner to read: "Redwood gives platform teams a predictable inference runtime that matches enterprise SLAs without building the entire stack."

Slide 2 — Who to involve (one-minute map)
- Quick list to surface: platform engineering, SRE, security/compliance, procurement (if reserved spend), and a feature owner for evals.
- Speaker prompt: Ask: "Which of those teams will own uptime and capacity SLAs for this project?"

Slide 3 — Signals we want to hear (qualifier checklist)
- Are you hitting concurrency limits with hosted APIs today? (yes/no)
- Do you need private network (VPC) access or air-gapped installs? (yes/no)
- Target p95 latency SLA for user-facing product? (ms)
- Expected steady-state TPS and burst profile? (tokens/sec or requests/min)
- Data residency / KMS/HSM requirement? (yes/no)
- Speaker note: capture free-form answers; these map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Slide 4 — Quick mapping: answers -> next step (annotated decision lanes)
- If "concurrency limits" or "cost spikes" -> reserved Dedicated sizing conversation.
- If "VPC or HSM required" -> Private deployment track and security questionnaire.
- If p95 < 200ms and < 1k concurrent -> Hosted API can often meet this; follow with latency profile and token distribution.
- Annotated seller line: "If multiple boxes checked, recommend a two-week pilot on Dedicated with a canary rollout."

Slide 5 — Short tech cheat sheet (for rapid objections)
- Latency lever: choose lower-latency model families, shorter seq lengths, enable KV cache for repeated prompts.
- Cost lever: quantization profiles + batching + prefix cache. Explain quickly: "Batching reduces per-token GPU overhead but increases tail latency; we can tune by route."
- Reliability lever: multi-region fallback + model variant fallback (e.g., smaller quantized model) for degraded capacity.
- Speaker note: have one concrete example (internal): "We reduced p95 from 480ms to 180ms by enabling KV cache + switching to a TGI-optimized kernel on our Dedicated pool."

Slide 6 — Demo checklist for a 10-minute show
- Pre-demo ask: share a representative prompt set and average token counts.
- Quick verification steps: API key with sample org scoped token, sample prompt set, approximate target RPS.
- Live demo script: 1) baseline hosted request latency, 2) show throughput with burst simulation, 3) toggle routing to a fallback small model to show graceful degradation.
- Failover highlight: show automatic fallthrough response in under 5s (annotated script and expected logs).

Slide 7 — Common technical objections and rebuttals (seller scripts)
- Objection: "We can host ourselves, why Redwood?"
  - Rebuttal: "We surface kernel/model combos tuned for throughput, autoscaling for steady/bursting, and pre-built KV caching that saves tokens. That reduces ops overhead so your team focuses on product signals not infra tuning."
- Objection: "Will private meet our compliance?"
  - Rebuttal: "We support customer-managed control planes, KMS/HSM integrations, and air-gapped on-prem packaging; we can supply architecture diagrams and a security questionnaire within 48 hours."
- Objection: "How do we avoid runaway cost?"
  - Rebuttal: "Reserved capacity + routing policies + quantization suggestions give a predictable unit-economics story; we show token-level cost breakdown in the Console."

Slide 8 — Pricing quickframe (talking points, not a quote)
- Hosted: pay-as-you-go per-token, good for fast POC and early low-throughput.
- Dedicated: commit monthly for predictable throughput; great when you run large production traffic or need isolation.
- Private: license + support for regulated workloads; separates control plane from infra.
- Speaker script: "Use this to set expectations, but for any real deal we will propose a committed usage plan after the pilot."

Slide 9 — Mini-case (2–3 bullets)
- Customer: fintech platform moved high-value routing to Dedicated, saved ~37% per-inference cost through batching and quantization and achieved a p95 of 220ms for session-based flows.
- Annotated ask: "If a customer cares about both cost and latency, we recommend starting Dedicated with a 60-day tuning window and defined SLOs."

Slide 10 — Next steps & playbook (what sellers should do after call)
- If Platform/SRE: request the sample prompt set + token histogram and propose a sizing call with solutions engineering.
- If Security/Compliance: route to the Private deployment packet and attach KMS/HSM integration FAQ.
- If Product/PM: schedule a 1-hour trial to validate quality regressions for the chosen model family.
- Speaker quick-close lines: always get a concrete metric (p95 latency target) and a sample payload distribution before the follow-up call.

Appendix — quick snippets sellers can paste into follow-up email
- "Thanks — to help us size a pilot, can you share: representative prompt set, average token per request, expected steady RPS and max burst RPS, and whether you require VPC/HSM? We'll use that to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and propose a short pilot plan."
- Technical inline snippet for SEs: curl example to exercise throughput and measure p95 (include placeholder).

Unresolved notes / TODOs in this draft:
- Add one slide with a minimal network architecture diagram for Private (ask infra for SVG).
- Replace the single internal latency example with an anonymized chart from our playbook.
- Request sample YAML for Dedicated sizing run from Solutions Engs.

Tone & style guidance for sellers:
- Keep it short, measurement-first, do not promise exact numbers without a pilot. Use plain comparators ("we expect X to Y improvement after pilot tuning").
- Avoid deep implementation conversations on first call; surface constraints and schedule a technical sizing call.

Files to attach in candidate follow-up packet (linked_artifacts above reference these):
- Security questionnaire PDF
- Dedicated sizing spreadsheet (sheet id in linked_artifacts)
- Sample pilot SOW template

End of deck.

Document history: authored by Priya Desai 2024-10-15; internal review with SEs Miguel and Ellen week of 2024-10-28; built from repeated field asks about quick qualification for ops buyers.
notes: Draft status: intended as field-first, annotated for seller scripts. Do not use as final contract language. Will iterate after SE feedback and with an anonymized latency chart replacement.
